messages:
alex: Quick note — onboarding Suzaku-7B (Mistral-like) into our int4 path. Hit an odd combo: multi-codepoint emoji tokenization drift + embedding/projection reorder after quantize. Repro and short logs below. Anyone seen this interplay before? :thinking:

alex: Minimal repro:
```bash
python export_model.py --model suzaku-7b --dtype fp16 --out suzaku_fp16.onnx
python quantize.py --in suzaku_fp16.onnx --out suzaku_int4.onnx --backend awq --apply-permute
python run_infer.py --model suzaku_int4.onnx --prompt "I \u2764\ufe0f pizza" --log-tokens
```

alex: Logs (sanitized):
```
# fp16 token ids: [11, 12879, 4, 2]
# int4 token ids: [11, 6534, 4, 2]
# embedding dot[0] diff: 0.003 -> 0.12
```

alex: Observations: token id for heart emoji changed and proj/embedding dot increased. Hypothesis: our quantizer inserted a permute/reshape targeting q/k/v projections assuming uniform head_dim; Suzaku has hetero head dims (mix of 64 and 48) due to a legacy adapter, so offsets get mangled. Also NFKC + byte-level pretokenizer routes multi-codepoint emoji into slightly different byte boundaries; if the permute runs before or changes embedding layout that can flip tokenization.

tanya: Can you paste tokenizer config and ONNX node names?

alex: Tokenizer snippet: normalizer: unicode_nfkc, pretokenizer: byte-level, emoji_policy: char_split. ONNX nodes include embed.weight, attn.q_proj/k_proj/v_proj, and a quantizer-inserted permute_proj_axes.

zach: permute_proj_axes is our AWQ shim to align proj order between Gemma/Mistral. If Suzaku uses nonuniform head dims a global reshape/transpose will mangle per-head offsets. Action: we should emit per-head reshape+transpose when head_dims are non-uniform. I'll draft a patch.

maria: Short-term mitigation: add a tokenizer pre-hook to canonicalize common multi-codepoint emoji sequences into single canonical codepoints for onboarding evals. Also add tokenization unit tests for multi-codepoint emoji.

ci-bot: CI job suzaku_int4_tokenize_check failed  token mismatch. https://ci.internal/3322

tanya: Run quantize with permute disabled (--no-permute) and compare tokens+logits to isolate permute vs rounding diffs.

alex: Did that: --no-permute yields matching token ids with FP16 but logits still show small RMS difference (~0.5% next-token prob). So two issues: permute caused tokenization mismatch; quant rounding shifts embeddings slightly which can affect sensitive tokens. My small bench (50 emoji prompts): fp16 vs int4 w/o permute exact match 96.8%, BLEU delta 0.6. With permute incorrect: exact match 88.4%, BLEU delta 3.9.

zach: PR plan: 1) quantizer: when head_dims non-uniform -> emit per-head reshape+transpose with explicit offsets; 2) add model-registry audit rule to flag hetero-head models so pipeline picks safe path by default; 3) add KV-cache index smoke tests because per-head transforms can shift KV layout.

maria: Tests: add tokenizer unit tests for multi-codepoint emoji normalization + a small generation smoke test used in CI for onboarding models.

tanya: When you open the PR, include minimal repro, CI link, and labels onboard/suzaku and quant/permute-fix. I'll coordinate a small Dedicated canary once merged.

alex: Opening PR now. Summary in PR: root cause = global permute + hetero head_dim assumption + tokenizer NFKC/byte-level edge-case for multi-codepoint emoji. Fixes = per-head permute/reshape path, tokenizer pre-hook collapse for onboarding, CI unit tests. :thumbsup:
